functions.signature: void Ui_DrawNumberRight(int value, char lead, char * suffix, int x, int y, int width, void * font, int colour)
functions.comment: Ui_DrawNumber, right-aligned inside width.

functions.name: Ui_DrawDelta
functions.signature: void Ui_DrawDelta(int value, int mode, byte * prefix, char * suffix, int x, int y, void * font, int colourPos, int colourNeg)
functions.comment: A signed number with a prefix and a suffix - and nothing at all when the value is zero and mode is 0, which is why the happiness and population panels have blank rows in a quiet season.

functions.name: Ui_NumberToBuffer
functions.signature: void Ui_NumberToBuffer(int value, int start, int forceSign)
functions.comment: Formats value into g_numberBuffer starting at index start, writing '-' or '+' at start and shifting when it does. Callers pass start = 1 so index 0 stays free for a sign character.

functions.name: Ui_DrawCount
functions.signature: void Ui_DrawCount(int value, int unitIndex, int x, int y, void * font, int colour)
functions.comment: A number followed by a noun from L2.eng group 8: index unitIndex when the value is 1 or -1, unitIndex + 1 otherwise. Group 8 is singular at even indices and plural at odd.

functions.name: Ui_DrawHappinessDelta
functions.signature: void Ui_DrawHappinessDelta(int value, int x, int y, void * font, int colourPos, int colourNeg)
functions.comment: Draws a bracketed signed number with the happiness face after it: a bracket, Ui_DrawDelta, g_miscCtySheet frame 0x17, a closing bracket.

functions.name: Ui_DrawUnitNoun
functions.signature: void Ui_DrawUnitNoun(int value, int unitIndex, int x, int y, void * font, int colour)
functions.comment: Just the group 8 noun, singular when the value is 1.

functions.name: Ui_DrawYear
functions.signature: void Ui_DrawYear(int year, int x, int y, int style)
functions.comment: A year with BC or AD from L2.eng group 26. style 3 prints the number alone, which is what the graph axes use.

functions.name: Ui_HistoryGraph
functions.signature: uint Ui_HistoryGraph(int x, int y, int mode)
functions.comment: The 402x155 history graph on the population and happiness panels. mode 0 reads g_countyHistory +0x00 (population, u32), mode 1 reads +0x04 (happiness, u8), walking g_historyLength turns from g_historyHead and wrapping at 400. Returns the peak, which the caller prints. Background from graphs.pl8.

functions.name: Res_LoadStatic
functions.comment: Loads the thirteen records of g_preloadTable into their fixed .data buffers - three palettes, five fonts, mouse.pl8, System2.pl8, Panels.pl8, l2.eng and vill_gd8.pl8. That table is the whole interface asset list.

functions.name: Res_LoadButtons
functions.comment: Loads system2.pl8 (skin 0) or system.pl8 (skin 1) into g_systemSheet. Same size and same 84-frame layout, but 69 of System2.pl8s frames are entirely index 0 and none of System.pl8s are, and the kingdom screens ask for skin 1 - so the county panels button art is System.pl8. docs/screens-county.md section 4.2.

functions.name: CountyStrip_Draw
functions.comment: The selected county's strip in the map sidebar: name, population, happiness, tax rate, ration achieved and the health thermometer for an owned county; frame 0x3A and the owner's name for one you do not hold. docs/screens-county.md section 2.

functions.name: CountyStrip_Click
functions.comment: The 2x2 hotspot over the county strip, and the only way to any of the four county panels: x 488..547 / y 182..211 population, x 568..629 / y 182..211 happiness, and the same two columns below y 212 for tax and rations. The dead band 548..567 is where the health thermometer is drawn.

functions.name: CountyStrip_JobClick
functions.comment: The sidebar's lower plate: farm jobs left of x 560, industry right of it. Sets g_jobPanelJob and opens screen 0x0F.

functions.name: Panel_Ration
functions.comment: The ration panel (screen 0x19). Draws L2.eng group 87 against county +0x15E (wanted), +0x15D (achieved, red when they differ), +0x09 (health band), +0x11 and +0x10 as happiness deltas, and the Fed / Eaten rows from +0x16C, +0x170, +0x174, +0x178 and +0x17C.

functions.name: Panel_RationSlider
functions.comment: The grain-to-livestock slider: caps from g_systemSheet frames 0x4A and 0x4B at x 200 and 324, a 100-pixel track from x 224 to 323, and the knob (frame 0x4C, 10 wide) at 220 + county +0x15F.

functions.name: Panel_JobDetail
functions.comment: The job popup (screen 0x0F) for g_jobPanelJob, 1..9 into L2.eng group 74. Draws the worker count with the group 8 noun for job*2 + 30, red when labour +0x00 is below +0x04 and a second colour when it is above +0x08 - which is what shows the labour record to be three integers a job, not one.

functions.name: Panel_JobIndustry
functions.comment: The mining, quarrying, wood and blacksmith bodies of the job popup. Maps jobs 5, 6, 7 and 8 to industry records 1, 3, 0 and 2, the same order the village artwork implies.

functions.name: Panel_JobGrain
functions.comment: The grain body of the job popup: store, fertility band, the event and weather effects on the store, and either what will be sown in spring or what is growing and when it is harvested. Nothing on it is clickable - the player never chooses how much to sow.

functions.name: Panel_JobCattle
functions.comment: The cattle body of the job popup: L2.eng group 77 calf births, cow deaths and the herd-crowding bands.

functions.name: Panel_JobReclamation
functions.comment: The field-reclamation body of the job popup: how many fields are being reclaimed and how many seasons to the next one.

functions.name: Panel_JobBlacksmith
functions.comment: The blacksmith body of the job popup, with smithy.pl8 and hearth.pl8 and the weapon's cost from g_weaponCost.

functions.name: Village_Draw
functions.comment: The village screen (screen 0x02): villani1/villani2/vill.pl8, villtops.pl8, and the weather and fertility lines when Advanced Farming is on. The scene starts at y = g_villageTopY.

functions.name: Village_DrawPeasants
functions.comment: Draws the eight peasant clusters at g_jobClusterOrigins + (0x40, g_villageTopY).

functions.name: Village_DrawCluster
functions.signature: void Village_DrawCluster(int cluster, int x, int y)
functions.comment: One cluster: up to 25 icons from g_peasantIcons at the offsets in g_peasantIconOffsets, each frame bumped by one while the cluster is the drag source.

functions.name: Village_Animate
functions.comment: Steps the village's animation counters and draws the animated overlays.

functions.name: Village_BoxSelect
functions.comment: Marks every peasant icon inside the rubber-band box, and abandons the whole selection if the box reaches into a second cluster. Leaves the cluster in g_villageDragCluster and the count in g_villageDragCount.

functions.name: Village_ClusterAt
functions.comment: Which of the eight clusters the pointer is over, 1-based, or 0.

functions.name: Labour_Move
functions.signature: void Labour_Move(int county, int fromCluster, int toCluster, int workers)
functions.comment: Moves workers between two labour slots of one county and re-runs the county's food and industry passes twice. The caller's count is selected icons times county +0xB8 (popBand), clamped to what the source slot holds - so one icon is one twenty-fifth of the population, rounded up.

functions.name: Job_SlotForCluster
functions.comment: Cluster to labour slot through g_jobClusterToSlot, with cluster 0 overridden from stone (5) to iron (4) when the county has industry 1's resource and not industry 3's. That single case pins industry 1 = iron and industry 3 = stone.

functions.name: Village_RebuildIcons
functions.comment: Rebuilds g_peasantIcons for one county: workers divided by popBand icons per cluster, with the surplus or shortfall against the slot's +0x04 and +0x08 drawn in a different frame.

functions.name: Tax_Increase
functions.comment: The tax panel's up arrow. Guards taxRate < 0x32 - the player's tax ceiling is 50, and this is where it lives.

functions.name: Tax_IncreaseCounty
functions.comment: Raises one county's tax rate by one, capped at 50, then Tax_RecomputePreview and a redraw.

functions.name: Tax_Decrease
functions.comment: The tax panel's down arrow. Guards taxRate != 0.

functions.name: Tax_DecreaseCounty
functions.comment: Lowers one county's tax rate by one, floored at 0.

functions.name: Tax_RecomputePreview
functions.comment: Recomputes one county's tax display: +0xC0 taxShown from population, the castle multiplier and the rate; +0x0F = 5 - rate; and +0x16 from g_taxHappinessOther[rate]. It is the only writer of +0x16 anywhere in the binary, so the empire tax happiness term is a table lookup rather than 5 - rate.

functions.name: Panels_RefreshAll
functions.comment: End of the season pipeline: Ration_Apply, the next-season preview and Tax_RecomputePreview for every county. This is the second Ration_Apply call docs/decisions.md C20 identified from the save.

functions.name: Ration_Increase
functions.comment: The ration panel's up arrow. Guards rationWanted < 5.

functions.name: Ration_IncreaseCounty
functions.comment: Raises one county's wanted ration by one, capped at 5, then re-applies rations and redraws.

functions.name: Ration_Decrease
functions.comment: The ration panel's down arrow. Guards rationWanted > 0.

functions.name: Ration_DecreaseCounty
functions.comment: Lowers one county's wanted ration by one, floored at 0.

functions.name: Ration_SliderClick
functions.comment: The grain-to-livestock slider's hit test: (200,220,24,24) steps down, (325,220,24,24) steps up, and (224,220,102,24) jumps to mouseX - 224. Clamped 0..100, and refused outright unless the county's owner is g_localPlayer.

functions.name: Ration_SetSplit
functions.signature: void Ration_SetSplit(int county, int split, int sweep)
functions.comment: Sets county +0x15F and re-runs the food pass; if the new split changes nothing it walks back towards the old value looking for one that does.

functions.name: Panel_OpenRation
functions.comment: Opens the ration panel (screen 0x19).

functions.name: Panel_OpenPopulation
functions.comment: Opens the population panel (screen 0x14).

functions.name: Panel_OpenHappiness
functions.comment: Opens the happiness panel (screen 0x16).

functions.name: Panel_OpenTax
functions.comment: Opens the tax panel (screen 0x15).

functions.name: Turn_End
functions.comment: The sidebar's full-width bottom button: ends the local player's turn by writing 999 into the realm record's +0x00.

functions.name: Sidebar_Button
functions.comment: The five buttons in the 162x30 strip at y 430, on g_uiHotspotId 1..5: the county's army (screen 0x17), the court (screen 0x09), send supplies (screen 0x18), and two more.

functions.name: Court_Draw
functions.comment: The court screen (0x09): L2.eng group 70 against the realm record - gold +0x118, iron +0x120, stone +0x128, wood +0x130, six weapon stocks from +0x140, army wages +0xFC and expected tax +0x15C.

functions.name: Field_SetType
functions.signature: void Field_SetType(uint county, int tile, int brush)
functions.comment: Repaints one map tile's field type for a county and re-runs its food passes. Called from a map click with the brush in g_uiHotspotId; this, not any county panel, is how fields are assigned.

functions.name: Diplo_Init
functions.comment: Clears every inbox and every realm-pair record at new game. The one place each field of the 16-byte pair record at realm +0x84 + other*0x10 is written, which is what makes the field map in docs/diplomacy.md a reading rather than a guess: standing = 5 for an in-play AI realm and 0 otherwise, allied/grudge/warningsSent/atWar/complimentsFrom/hasMail = 0, bestGift = 0, helpPriceMultiple = 1.

functions.name: Diplo_Post
functions.signature: void Diplo_Post(int from, int to, int kind, int gold, unsigned char county)
functions.comment: The only writer of g_diploInbox. Fills the first free of five slots; bumps the recipient pair record's complimentsFrom when kind == 1; sets hasMail; and moves the gold immediately, clamped to what the sender holds - a gift is spent when it is posted, not when it is answered.

functions.name: Diplo_AnswerInbox
functions.comment: AI turn step 1. Walks the realm's five inbox slots, dispatching kind 0..6 to the seven reply handlers, then zeroes all five slots and all six hasMail bytes. An inbox is emptied every turn whether or not it was full, and a human realm never runs this because the AI turn machine is skipped for it.

functions.name: Diplo_ClearInboxes
functions.comment: Zeroes all 6 x 5 inbox slots. Called by Diplo_Init.

functions.name: Diplo_ReplyGift
functions.signature: void Diplo_ReplyGift(int me, int them, int gold)
functions.comment: Kind 0. Three tiers against best + T/2 and best + T, where T = personality +0x08 and best = pair.bestGift: L2.eng group 173 and standing -8, group 172 and +5, group 171 and +10. Then bestGift = max(bestGift, gold), so the bar ratchets and each gift must beat the last.

functions.name: Diplo_ReplyCompliment
functions.comment: Kind 1. On pair.complimentsFrom, which Diplo_Post incremented and nothing ever resets: 1 -> group 174 and standing +15, 2 -> group 175 and +8, 3 or more -> group 176 and -4. Group 176 is 'You are boring me now with your groveling letters.'

functions.name: Diplo_ReplyInsult
functions.signature: void Diplo_ReplyInsult(unsigned int me, unsigned int them)
functions.comment: Kind 2. Breaks any alliance between the two, standing -20, replies with L2.eng group 177.

functions.name: Diplo_ReplyAllianceOffer
functions.comment: Kind 3. Refuses with group 196 if already at war, 197 if I already have an ally, 178 otherwise; accepts with 179 and Diplo_FormAlliance. Accepts outright at standing >= 11, refuses outright below -10, and in between rolls g_rand7B < standing*3 + 45 out of 128. Accept +4, plain refusal -2, 'cannot' refusal -1.

functions.name: Diplo_ReplyAllianceEnd
functions.signature: void Diplo_ReplyAllianceEnd(unsigned int me, unsigned int them)
functions.comment: Kind 4. Breaks the alliance and takes standing -15. Sends no message at all - terminating an alliance from the diplomacy screen is silent. Group 182 'Broken alliance.' comes from Diplo_Offend instead, when an act rather than a letter breaks one.

functions.name: Diplo_ReplyHelpRequest
functions.signature: void Diplo_ReplyHelpRequest(int me, unsigned int them, unsigned int county)
functions.comment: Kind 5. Refuses with group 183 (+1 grudge) unless they are my ally, my gold is at least personality +0x30, and standing is at least 10; then g_rand7B < standing*4 accepts with group 184 and marches for free, otherwise group 185 demands personality[+0x0C] * pair.helpPriceMultiple gold.

functions.name: Diplo_ReplyAttackRequest
functions.signature: void Diplo_ReplyAttackRequest(int me, unsigned int them, unsigned int county)
functions.comment: Kind 6, identical in shape to Diplo_ReplyHelpRequest but with groups 186/187/188, a +2 grudge on refusal and half the acceptance odds (g_rand7B < standing*2).

functions.name: Diplo_FormAlliance
functions.comment: Sets pair.allied = 1 and pair.grudge = 0 both ways and realm +0x81 on both sides. Six bytes; that is the whole of what an alliance is. realm +0x81 is a single byte, so a realm has at most one ally.

functions.name: Diplo_BreakAlliance
functions.signature: void Diplo_BreakAlliance(unsigned int a, unsigned int b)
functions.comment: Clears pair.allied and realm +0x81 on whichever sides point at the other. Does not touch standing - the caller applies that.

functions.name: Diplo_ReconcileAlliances
functions.comment: Called from Turn_Tick. Rebuilds the allied matrix from the realms' ally bytes and drops any pairing that is one-sided or whose partner has been eliminated.

functions.name: Diplo_ActionAllowed
functions.signature: int Diplo_ActionAllowed(unsigned int actor, unsigned int target)
functions.comment: Returns 0 when target is actor's ally - adding 1 to the ally's grudge instead - or when the two are the same realm; 1 otherwise. Gates the offence hook, which is why hostile acts against an ally cost grudge rather than standing.

functions.name: Diplo_PayForHelp
functions.signature: void Diplo_PayForHelp(int ally, int payer, unsigned char county, int price)
functions.comment: Moves price gold from payer to ally if they can afford it, increments pair.helpPriceMultiple so the next purchase costs more, takes standing -4, and sets the ally's warTarget (realm +0xE8) to the county. Called with price 0 when the ally agreed for free, and from the pay prompt otherwise.

functions.name: Diplo_Offend
functions.signature: void Diplo_Offend(unsigned int offended, unsigned int offender, char amount)
functions.comment: The single hook every relationship-damaging act goes through. If the offender was an ally: break it, set pair.atWar unless the offended lord is 4 (the Bishop), set warTarget, Diplo_OffendAll(offender, 15), send group 182, and add 15 to the penalty. Then standing -= amount, clamped to [-30,+30]. Once standing bottoms out at -30 against a human it walks pair.warningsSent: group 189, then 190, then 191 and war.

functions.name: Diplo_OffendAll
functions.comment: Lowers every other realm's standing towards this one. Only reached from Diplo_Offend when an alliance is betrayed - the one act in the game that costs reputation with third parties.

functions.name: Diplo_PickAllyCandidate
functions.comment: Picks the best-ranked realm that is in play, not ranked 1st, unallied, not already being courted, not at war with this one, and above standing -10. Returns 0 for none.

functions.name: Diplo_DefaultTarget
functions.comment: Sets g_diploTarget to the first in-play realm that is not the local player, or 0.

functions.name: AI_Diplomacy
functions.comment: AI turn step 2, and the real diplomacy driver. Heals standing by +1 a turn towards every NON-HUMAN realm, so an AI's opinion of a human player never recovers. Then ages the alliance grudge and breaks the alliance past personality +0x10; then, from year 1269 and if not ranked 1st, courts Diplo_PickAllyCandidate's pick every personality +0x14 turns - silently against an AI, with group 180 against a human. Its ally-is-winning tier ladder has its comparisons inverted, so two of its three tiers are unreachable.

functions.name: AI_Taunt
functions.comment: AI turn step 13. Not 'offer an alliance or break one' as docs/kingdom.md 3.2 said: a taunt timer. A realm ranked better than 2nd and holding more than 39 percent of the map sends group 193 'How are you doing?' to every human after 8 turns; afterwards, above 27 percent, it sends group 192 'Helpful advice.' to the last-placed realm if that realm is human and not its ally.

functions.name: AI_BuildCastles
functions.comment: AI turn step 6. For each owned, castle-less county above personality +0xC8 population, and while the realm has fewer than personality +0x90 builds in progress, orders the largest castle type whose gold threshold at personality +0xCC..+0xDC the treasury clears. A zero threshold means that type is not offered to that lord. The Bishop reaches the royal castle at 2,000 gold where the Knight needs 10,000, and the Baron and Countess never build one.

functions.name: AI_EmergencyWeapons
functions.comment: An AI down to one county before year 1273 is handed 100 each of weapon types 3 and 4 if its lord is 4 (the Bishop), or 100 of weapon type 0 if its lord is 3 (the Countess). The Knight and the Baron get nothing. Returns 1 if it granted anything.

functions.name: Msg_Enqueue
functions.signature: void Msg_Enqueue(int from, int to, int group, int variant, unsigned char category, unsigned char county, unsigned char spare, int payload)
functions.comment: The general notification path, 144 call sites. Builds a 24-byte record at g_messageCompose and copies it into the 50-slot ring g_messageQueue. The group is an L2.eng group id and the variant selects the string within it (drawn as variant + 1, past the group's label at index 0). Enqueues only when the recipient is realm 0 or the local player - the three isHuman branches all compute that same predicate.

functions.name: Msg_EnqueueCurrent
functions.comment: Pushes whatever is already in g_messageCompose onto the ring. The tail half of Msg_Enqueue, reached directly by callers that filled the compose record themselves.

functions.name: Msg_Reset
functions.comment: Clears the message ring, its head and tail and the pending flag.

functions.name: Msg_Pump
functions.comment: Pulls one record from g_messageQueueTail, unpacks it into g_messageGroup, g_messageVariant and friends, starts the 2000-tick g_messageTimer and calls Msg_DrawWindow. Runs only on screens 0x00, 0x27, 0x29 and 0x0F with job panel 8.

functions.name: Msg_DrawWindow
functions.comment: Draws the message window. The layout is chosen by the record's category byte; the text is Eng_DrawString(group, 0) for the heading and (group, variant + 1) for the body, and Msg_PlayVoice is called with the same (group, variant). 10,915 bytes, read here only for its text and voice lookups.

functions.name: Msg_PlayVoice
functions.comment: Maps an L2.eng group to a .wav filename in one of three tables. Groups 170..197 - the diplomatic letters - index g_msgVoiceLord by (group - 170) * 0x100 + variant * 0x10, giving Kt/Bn/Ct/Bp <group>_<1..4>.wav for the Knight, Baron, Countess and Bishop. Groups 100..169 and 200..284 have one system file each. All 448 lord files exist in the install.

functions.name: Diplo_DrawScreen
functions.comment: Screen 0x0B, 'the other lords'. Loads faces.pl8, draws one lord card per rival, and draws L2.eng group 72 as the action menu in one of four layouts held in g_diploMenuState: no ally (items 2-5), allied to this lord (2,3,4,6,7,8), allied elsewhere (2,3,4), or a message already pending from them (item 24 alone).

functions.name: Diplo_DrawLordCard
functions.comment: One rival's card: portrait from faces.pl8 frame lord*3-3 (frame 12 for a human), shield, name from g_playerNames, allied / at-war / mail icons, and a 10 x 63 standing thermometer whose three colours break at standing >= +11 and <= -11 - exactly the two thresholds Diplo_ReplyAllianceOffer decides on.

functions.name: Diplo_SendClicked
functions.comment: The diplomacy screen's Send button. Validates the county for kinds 5 and 6 (refusals are L2.eng groups 240-244) and the target's existing alliance for kind 3 (group 219), copies the drafted letter into the player's g_diploLetter slot, then calls Diplo_Post - or, in multiplayer, issues net command 0x48 or 0x49 instead.

functions.name: Diplo_PayHelpClicked
functions.comment: The pay-for-help prompt's accept button: Diplo_PayForHelp(myAlly, me, g_diploHelpCounty, g_diploHelpPrice).

functions.name: Net_DiploPost
functions.comment: Network command handler - it has no callers in the decompilation, so it is dispatched from a command table. Calls Diplo_Post from the arguments the net layer unpacked; FUN_00448339 is the gold-transfer half.

functions.name: Eng_Seek
functions.comment: Walks L2.eng to the (group, index) string and leaves the pointer in g_engCursor, exactly as docs/formats/eng.md 1.3 describes. New-game setup calls Eng_Seek(7, realm[+0x07]) and copies 16 bytes into g_playerNames - the game naming its own lords out of group 7, which is what fixes 1 = The Knight, 2 = The Baron, 3 = The Countess, 4 = The Bishop.

functions.name: Units_Tick
functions.comment: Per-frame unit driver: walks slots 1..150 of g_units and dispatches each through g_unitTickTable[type]. Type 0 or above 5 clears the record. Slot 5 of that table is NULL while the dispatcher accepts type 5, so a type-5 unit would call address 0; nothing spawns one.

functions.name: Units_ResetMoves
functions.comment: Start of season: clears moveState (+0x14C) and movesUsed (+0x153) on all 150 unit slots. Called from turn phase 7.

functions.name: Army_Tick
functions.comment: The type-1 (army) tick. Writes moveAllowance (+0x154) = 15 unconditionally, picks the sprite bank by men (<301 -> 0x48, <601 -> 0x60, else 0x78) plus 3*facing plus the walk frame, calls Unit_EnterCounty when the tile county differs from +0x10, and steps the mover.

functions.name: Unit_Step
functions.comment: Walks one unit along its stored path. Stops when movesUsed reaches moveAllowance. Dispatches Transport_Deliver, Unit_TrampleTile and Unit_BurnDwelling from Unit_TryEnterTile's return code.

functions.name: Unit_StepOnce
functions.comment: One animation tick of a move: accumulates +0x149 to 16, then calls Unit_NeighbourTile and charges movesUsed +1 on a road (+0x14D set) or +3 otherwise.

functions.name: Unit_NeighbourTile
functions.comment: Maps a direction 0..7 to the neighbouring tile offset with edge-of-map guards and hands it to Unit_TryEnterTile.

functions.name: Unit_TryEnterTile
functions.comment: Classifies the target tile and returns a code: occupied -> Unit_EnterOccupiedTile; road (plane0 0x01) -> 3; county town (0x40) -> 5; castle (0x80) -> 6; dwelling plot (0x10) -> 7; farm field (0x20) -> 8; otherwise 1. The 0x40 and 0x80 labels were swapped here until decisions.md C25; the codes themselves are unchanged. The entry guard that clears bit 0x80 when the terrain is 0x14 is County_FindCastleTile's stamp, which is how a built castle stops blocking its owner.

functions.name: Unit_MoveInFacing
functions.comment: Commits one step of g_movingUnit in the facing it has already been given: erases the sprite, plays the per-kind movement sound (army 0x0C, mob 5, merchant/transport 0x0B), adds the eight compass deltas to x, y and tileOffset (+-1 tile, +-8 and +-0x200 bytes of g_tiles), redraws, then sets onRoad from bit 0x01 of the tile's plane-0 flag byte. Unit_StepOnce is the caller: it charges the move (3 off-road, 1 on-road), writes facing, and calls this. [D] - the check that could have failed is that all eight cases are exactly the eight compass deltas and that tileOffset stays (y*64+x)*8 in every one of them; a case that disagreed would have shown up as a ninth delta.

functions.name: Unit_CrossField
functions.comment: A step onto a farm field: charges 3 extra moves and, when the tile's county is not the unit's own, worsens diplomacy by 10 (human owners only) and calls County_DestroyField. Total cost 6, which is what g_moveCost holds for a field.

functions.name: County_DestroyField
functions.comment: Removes one field: a grain field takes crop * (100/fieldsSown) percent off county +0x244 and decrements +0x201; a pasture takes the same fraction off the herd and decrements +0x200. The tile is repainted bare.

functions.name: County_TileIsField
functions.comment: True when the tile terrain is in 2..0x16, the range County_DestroyField will act on.

functions.name: Move_BuildCostMap
functions.comment: Rebuilds the 64x64 i16 campaign movement cost map g_moveCost from the map planes: 1 road, 3 open ground, 6 a standing field, 100 castle/settlement/plot, 0 impassable. Run once a season from turn phase 7.

functions.name: Move_FloodFill
functions.comment: Fills the campaign distance field (g_moveDistLocal for the local player, g_moveDistOther otherwise) outward from a tile using g_moveCost. Assumed cost-weighted breadth-first; the body was not read.
functions.signature: void Move_FloodFill(int who, int x, int y, int mode)

functions.name: Path_CopyToUnit
functions.comment: Copies g_pathBuf[slot] into the unit record: length to +0x1C and up to 150 (x, y) pairs to +0x1D. 150 * 2 = 300 bytes, ending exactly at +0x149.

functions.name: Path_ClearBuf
functions.comment: Zeroes one of the shared campaign path buffers and its length.

functions.name: Unit_OrderMove
functions.comment: Gives a unit a destination: rebuild the cost map, flood-fill from the unit, extract the path, copy it into the record, set moveState = 2 and the destination x/y.
functions.signature: void Unit_OrderMove(int who, int unit, int x, int y, char mode)

functions.name: Path_MarkPreviewTiles
functions.comment: Sets bit 0x40 of byte +2 of every runtime tile record along the local player's path buffer. Map_DrawPathMarker draws the gold path balls on exactly those tiles.

functions.name: Map_HoverUnitTarget
functions.comment: Runs the campaign pathfinder to the tile under the cursor and collects what a click there would do. When moveAllowance minus movesUsed is less than the path distance it zeroes every collected target, so an out-of-range click does nothing.

functions.name: Unit_EnterCounty
functions.comment: Called when a unit crosses a county border: sets +0x10, fires County_GreetArmy for a neutral county, and for an owned one sends message 0xAA (L2.eng group 170, the sixteen invasion taunts) when that county is the unit's declared destination.

functions.name: County_GreetArmy
functions.comment: Picks a neutral county's reaction to an army entering: happiness below 10 -> msg 0x82, below 30 -> 0x83, otherwise by the army as a percentage of the county population - 100 or more -> 0x83, 50..99 -> 0x84, 20..49 -> 0x85, under 20 -> 0x86 (L2.eng group 134, the border-violation message). The bigger the army the politer the reply.

functions.name: Army_RecountCountyTroops
functions.comment: Zeroes county +0x198 and +0x19C for all 16 counties, then adds every non-garrisoned type-1 or type-2 unit's men to the friendly or enemy total of the county it stands in (an ally, by realm +0x81, counts friendly), and re-runs Ration_Apply for every county.

functions.name: Army_Starve
functions.comment: Once a season from Wages_PayAll, and only when Army foraging is on. An army is fed when its men are fewer than Food_Available(county), or when it is garrisoned; otherwise +0x155 counts up, raising messages 0x116/0x117/0x118 (L2.eng 278/279/280), deserting 10 percent a season from the second, and destroying the army at 5.

functions.name: Army_Desert
functions.comment: Takes 10 percent off each of the seven troop counts (only where the count exceeds 10) and subtracts the same total from +0x168. Used by starvation and by bankruptcy stages 2..4.

functions.name: Levy_SetPercent
functions.comment: The raise-army slider: men = Pct(population, pct), happiness cost = g_armyHappinessCost[pct] plus county +0x2F4, clamped 0..100, then the percentage is walked back until county happiness minus the cost is at least 1. This is what indexes g_armyHappinessCost.

functions.name: Levy_Init
functions.comment: Zeroes the realm's 8-slot levy basket, seeds slots 1..6 with the realm's weapon stockpiles (realm +0x140 + (t-1)*4) and puts the levied headcount in slot 0 (unequipped peasants) and slot 7 (the total).

functions.name: Levy_ConsumeWeapons
functions.comment: Subtracts each levy basket slot 1..6 from the realm's matching weapon stock, then re-runs the labour allocator.

functions.name: Levy_DebitPopulation
functions.comment: Subtracts the levy total from county +0x24 (population) and +0x38 (the army line on the population panel).

functions.name: Army_Create
functions.comment: Spawns a type-1 unit on a free road or open tile of the county and fills it from the levy basket: men to +0x168, slots 0..6 to +0x16C, the year to +0x164, the county's happiness to +0x166 as morale, a name from Army_PickName, optionally a mercenary band; then debits happiness and county +0x15 and sets the county levy surcharge +0x2F4 to 15.
functions.signature: int Army_Create(int realm, int county, int hireMercs, int happinessCost)

functions.name: Army_PickName
functions.comment: Picks the least-used of the realm's 24 army-name slots at realm +0x2D and adds 2 to its counter. The names are L2.eng groups 94..98, 24 per lord.

functions.name: Army_Destroy
functions.comment: Frees an army: releases its garrison or siege link, decrements its name-slot counter, clears the unit record and recomputes the realm's wage bill.

functions.name: Army_Combine
functions.comment: Merges one army into another when the combined men are under 1501 and at most one of them carries mercenaries (otherwise message 0xA7, L2.eng 167). Sums men, the seven troop counts and the three siege-engine records, and keeps the lower movesUsed.

functions.name: Army_StrengthScore
functions.comment: Sum of troops[t] times g_troopStrengthWeight[t] over the seven campaign troop types plus the mercenary band, plus 20 when non-zero.

functions.name: Army_Garrison
functions.comment: Puts an army inside a county's castle: checks the combined men against the garrison cap for the castle type, writes county +0x1BC and unit +0x198, moves the unit onto the castle tile and charges 5 moves. Over the cap it sets unit +0x1A to 2 and refuses.

functions.name: Army_BeginSiege
functions.comment: Starts a siege if the county has a garrison, its castle is not under construction and it is not already besieged. Opens screen 0x1D for a human owner.

functions.name: Siege_Link
functions.comment: Sets unit +0x199 to the besieged county and the garrison's +0x19A back to the besieger, then runs Siege_Prepare.

functions.name: Siege_Prepare
functions.comment: Clears the three siege-engine build records at +0x182. For an AI owner it also hard-codes the order from the lord's personality record at 0x004D8AF8: two towers by default, or four towers, one ram, or three catapults plus a late ram against a large castle.

functions.name: Siege_RecomputeBuildTime
functions.comment: Recomputes each engine record's percent complete from work done over g_siegeEngineWork[e] times the count, and writes ceil(remaining work / men) into +0x19C - the seasons the siege preparation screen prints.

functions.name: Siege_BuildTick
functions.comment: One season of siege-engine construction: spreads the army's men evenly over the incomplete engine types, spills the remainder onto whichever is still short, and returns 1 when +0x19C reaches 0.

functions.name: Siege_StartPhase
functions.comment: Start of turn phase 2: breaks garrison and besieger links that no longer agree, then re-prepares every besieging army.

functions.name: Army_PrepareForBattle
functions.comment: Fills the battle-only troop slots just before a battle: mode 4 copies the three siege-engine counts into +0x17A/+0x17C/+0x17E (troop types 7, 8, 9); mode 0 sets +0x180 (oil, type 10) to 1, 2, 3, 4 or 6 by castle type 1..5.

functions.name: Army_ClearBattleSlots
functions.comment: Zeroes the battle-only troop slots +0x17A, +0x17C, +0x17E and +0x180 after a battle.

functions.name: Battle_ReturnToCampaign
functions.comment: Applies a battle result to the campaign: charges the winner moves (+8, or all but one for a human owner), clears garrison and siege links, flips a captured county, and destroys the loser - except under autocalc, where an army left with 50 or more men only has its siege lifted. Diplomacy takes a 20-point hit.

functions.name: Mercenary_Init
functions.comment: Once at new game: sets the band count from g_mercBandCountByCounties[g_countyCount] clamped to 1..12 and copies g_mercMen, g_mercTroopType, g_mercStartCounty, g_mercPeriod, g_mercPrice and g_mercWage into g_mercBands.

functions.name: Mercenary_AdvanceAll
functions.comment: Once a season: every unhired band clears its offer, counts its timer down and steps one county along, wrapping at g_countyCount; at zero it offers itself in that county and reloads. Then each county's +0x1AD caches the first band offered there.

functions.name: Mercenary_OfferInCounty
functions.comment: Returns the first unhired band whose offered-county field equals this county, or 0.

functions.name: Mercenary_Hire
functions.comment: Attaches a band to a newly created army: writes +0x195, +0x196 and +0x197, adds the men to +0x168, marks the band hired, debits the realm's gold by the band price and clears the county offer.

functions.name: Mercenary_Release
functions.comment: Removes an army's mercenary band: subtracts its men from +0x168, clears the three fields and frees the band for hire again. Used on disband and by bankruptcy stage 1.

functions.name: Screen_RaiseArmy
functions.comment: The raise-army screen: L2.eng group 69 over the levy slider, the six weapon stocks from realm +0x140, the happiness cost, and the mercenary offer for county +0x1AD - count and nationality from g_mercBands, the hire price, and men/2 as the seasonal wage.

functions.name: Screen_SplitArmyRows
functions.comment: The eight rows of the army-division screen (L2.eng group 17): troop types 0..6 from the levy basket in two columns, then row 7 as the mercenary band, then the two Total men lines.

functions.name: Screen_SiegePrep
functions.comment: The siege preparation screen (0x1D): L2.eng group 83, the seasons remaining from +0x19C, and a count plus a percent-complete bar for each of the three siege-engine records at +0x182, +0x188 and +0x18E.

functions.name: County_PlaceResourceSites
functions.comment: At load, scans the county for Town-bank tiles (runtime byte +2 masked with 0x1C equals 0x0C) and turns plane-2 descriptor 30, 0 and 20 into the iron, stone and wood industry sites: sets has_resource at +0x295 + c*0x18, stores the tile, and writes terrain 1, 4 and 10. This is where a county's resources come from - the map, not the county record.

functions.name: County_PlaceBlacksmith
functions.comment: Places the weapons industry site (record 2) on the plain tile of the county nearest one of its farm fields. The blacksmith is derived rather than authored, which is why every county has one.

functions.name: Move_ExtractPath
functions.signature: int Move_ExtractPath(int who, int x, int y)
functions.comment: The campaign path extractor (distinct from the battle's Path_Extract at 0x00472392). Greedy descent down a campaign distance field from (x, y) back to the source, appending (x, y) pairs into g_pathBuf[who] with the count in g_pathLen[who]. On a cost-1 road tile it steps the direction index by 2, orthogonals only, and falls back to all eight when that finds nothing.

functions.name: Labour_Allocate
functions.comment: The labour allocator, and the only writer of the nine job records. Splits the population into a farm half and an industry half by county +0x08, gives each job Pct(half, +0x130 + job*4) people or as many as its useful ceiling (+0xC4 + job*12 + 8) allows, walks the leftovers round the jobs with room - grain twice and cattle three times before reclamation once; wood, stone, iron and blacksmith once each before castle building - and drops the remainder into Idle townsfolk. Reproduced in l2-kingdom::labour; all fourteen counties of lastturn.sav come back exactly.

functions.name: Labour_AllocateAll
functions.comment: Labour_Allocate for counties 1..g_countyCount. Season_Advance calls it twice: after Castle_BuildTick and before Migration_UpdateAll, and again after FUN_00448D16 before Panels_RefreshAll.

functions.name: Labour_RecomputeIndustryShare
functions.comment: Rewrites county +0x08 from what was actually assigned: PctOf(pop - grain - cattle - reclamation - idle + idle/2, pop). Half the idle count is treated as industry.

functions.name: Labour_RecomputeShares
functions.comment: Rewrites the eight percentages at +0x130 + job*4 from the worker counts, in two groups - jobs 0..2 and jobs 3..7 - each renormalised to exactly 100 by giving the rounding remainder to the group's largest share. Its two indexed loops are what fix the array layout.

functions.name: Labour_DefaultShares
functions.comment: Farm 33/50/17 and all of the industry share on wood. Both halves sum to 100, which is the invariant that identifies the array.

functions.name: Labour_DefaultSharesBuilt
functions.comment: The same farm 33/50/17, with industry 40/15/15/15/15 - castle building favoured. Also sums to 100 in both halves. Which of the two setters a county gets is not traced.

functions.name: County_Reset
functions.comment: Sets every county up for a new game: population 150, popBand, ration 3, split 100, tax 50, industry share 25, then Labour_DefaultShares, clears all nine labour records to {0,0,0}, and runs the estimates and Labour_Allocate.

functions.name: Grain_LabourEstimate
functions.comment: Walks workers = 0..population calling Grain_Sow / Grain_Grow / Grain_Harvest, and stores the first count that reaches the best result in both the wanted floor (+0xC8) and the useful ceiling (+0xCC) of labour record 0. Also fills the grain panel's forecast fields.

functions.name: Herd_LabourEstimate
functions.comment: Walks workers = 0..population through Herd_BirthsAndDeaths. Writes the first staffing at which births less deaths stops being negative - or the least-bad one if it never does - to the cattle record's wanted floor (+0xD4), and the staffing that maximises it to the useful ceiling (+0xD8).

functions.name: Industry_LabourEstimate
functions.signature: void Industry_LabourEstimate(int county, int industry, int slot, int baseEfficiency, int divisor)
functions.comment: Fills one industry's labour record: wanted floor -1 always, useful ceiling 0 when the county has no such resource, the output-maximising worker count for weapons, and 100,000 - effectively unbounded - for iron, stone and wood. Called four times from FUN_004485A5 as (1,4,15,1) (3,5,15,2) (0,6,20,1) (2,7,15,4), which is the same job-and-divisor mapping l2-kingdom::tables holds.

functions.name: County_RefreshEstimates
functions.comment: The seven estimate passes that fill every labour record's floor and ceiling: crowding, Field_ReclaimEstimate, Grain_LabourEstimate, Herd_LabourEstimate, four Industry_LabourEstimate calls and Castle_BuildEstimate.

functions.name: Village_GridAt
functions.comment: Which peasant cluster a point on the village is over, 1-based and clamped to 8, from an 8-pixel grid: (&DAT_00542CF8)[((x-0x40)>>3) + ((y-g_villageTopY)>>3) * 0x2D]. That is vill_gd8.pl8 plus its 24-byte header - 45 x 40 cells covering x 0x40..0x1A8 and y top..top+0x140, and the shipped file is 1,824 bytes exactly.

functions.name: Village_BandStart
functions.comment: Arms the rubber band on a press inside x 0..0x1FF, y top..top+0x178, and returns 1 - moving the interface to screen 0x05 - once the pointer is 9 or more pixels from where it went down. Below nine it is still a click.

functions.name: Village_BandRelease
functions.comment: Screen 0x05 leaves on the button being released: 2 to screen 0x06 when the band caught somebody, 1 back to the village when it did not.

functions.name: Village_Drop
functions.comment: Screen 0x06's drop. Village_GridAt names the target cluster, the carried icon count is multiplied by county +0xB8 and clamped to what the source job holds, and Labour_Move does the rest. Dropping on the source cluster puts them back.

functions.name: Village_ClickJob
functions.comment: A click that never became a drag: Village_GridAt names the cluster and g_jobPanelJob becomes its labour slot plus one, which opens the job popup (screen 0x0F). FUN_0045183A refuses only cluster 0, and only for a county with neither a quarry nor a mine.

functions.name: Village_ClusterHasJob
functions.comment: Whether a cluster has a job to open. Only cluster 0 can say no, and only when the county has neither industry 3's stone nor industry 1's ore.

functions.name: Village_FillCluster
functions.signature: void Village_FillCluster(int county, int cluster, int normal, int other)
functions.comment: Turns one cluster's two icon counts into g_peasantIcons values. `other` is negative for a shortfall against the job's wanted floor and positive for a surplus past its useful ceiling; cluster 6, Idle townsfolk, is always drawn in the surplus icon.

functions.name: Map_Click
functions.comment: The campaign map's left-click dispatcher, and the only writer of g_screenId = 2 in the whole binary. Map_PickTile then Map_ResolvePick, then: a picked unit of type 1 that is yours opens its orders or siege preparation (screen 0x1D); one of type 3 that is yours opens the merchant (screen 0x08); otherwise the tile's own flags decide - g_pickedTileFlags bit 0x80 toggles the industry the building belongs to (Industry_ToggleFromMap), bit 0x40 opens the VILLAGE (screen 0x02), bit 0x20 opens screen 0x04. A county that is not yours gets Msg_Enqueue group 0x70 instead. The village branch centres the map on the county's town tile (+0x70) and runs one Map_DrawFrame before setting the screen - which is only worth doing because the map stays visible behind the village. docs/decisions.md C22.

functions.name: Map_ResolvePick
functions.comment: Turns the picked tile into the four things Map_Click branches on: g_pickedTileCounty from the county plane, g_pickedCountyOwner from that county's +0x05, g_pickedTileFlags from the attribute plane at 0x00522F91, and g_pickedTileGraphic from g_tiles. Then masks off three flag/graphic combinations that would otherwise be hotspots.

functions.name: Industry_ToggleFromMap
functions.comment: Clicking an industry building on the campaign map switches that industry on or off: it XORs the enable byte at +0x297 + industry*0x18 - the byte Labour_Allocate gates each mining job on - and maps the industry to its labour slot (0 wood -> 6, 1 iron -> 4, 2 weapons -> 7, 3 stone -> 5). Argument 4 is castle building instead, and toggles +0x1B0. Map_Click picks the argument from a ladder on g_pickedTileGraphic: 0..3 iron, 4..6 stone, 7..9 weapons, 10..12 wood, 13..20 nothing, 21+ castle.

functions.name: Screen_BattlePrompt
functions.comment: Screen 0x12: the 'a battle is to be fought' prompt. Draws L2.eng group 80 heading 0, or 7 'The Siege commences.' when g_battleIsSiege; then group 80 string 1 'Will you take the field?', 2 'Your opponent has the choice' or 3 'The opponents are deciding', selected by DAT_005533D0 (who owns the choice). County name from group 100 at g_scenarioIndex*20 + the battle county, the two lords' names from g_playerNames (group 99 string 0 '"The people."' for owner 6), and both army rosters via FUN_004224E7(g_battleArmyA, g_battleArmyB). Opened by FUN_004A7158 and its sibling, which play s080_01/02/03.wav on the same DAT_005533D0 - the WAV is named after the L2.eng group.

functions.name: Screen_BattleResult
functions.comment: Screen 0x13: the battle result report. Same layout as Screen_BattlePrompt with an OK button, L2.eng group 81 heading 0 'The Battle is decided.' or 8 'The siege is over.' under g_battleIsSiege, and the rosters redrawn in mode 1. Reached only after Battle_ReturnToCampaign has already been applied, so it reports rather than decides.

functions.name: TileInfo_Draw
functions.comment: The 'what is this tile' panel. Switches on the plane-0 flag byte in DAT_005440B0 (a copy of runtime tile +1) and picks a heading, a description paragraph and an icon frame out of L2.eng group 30: bit 0x01 -> 1 'Road.' + 0x17, 0x04 -> 3 'Sea.' + 0x18, 0x08 -> 4 'Mountain.'/5 'Woodland.', 0x10 -> 48 'Village'/50 'Ruined village.', 0x20 -> the farm-field table at 0x004D2EC8, 0x40 -> 7 'County town.' + 0x1B, 0x80 -> the resource sites (9 mine, 10 quarry, 11 lumber mill, 82 blacksmith) or the castle (8, or 14/15 for under construction/repair). Delegates to TileInfo_DrawGrain, TileInfo_DrawHerd and TileInfo_DrawCastle. Every heading pairs with the matching description, which is what fixes the bit meanings - see decisions.md C25 for the 0x40/0x80 correction this forced.

functions.name: TileInfo_DrawGrain
functions.comment: The grain half of TileInfo_Draw. Prints fertility from L2.eng group 22 indexed by (county +0x208 + 100) / 29 - seven strings for a -100..+100 range, which is exactly how many group 22 has - then sacks sown, the yield at g_grainYieldPerSack, and group 77's grain-store lines 0x18 'No outside factors affected stored grain.', 0x19 'eaten by rats.', 0x1A 'found as surplus.'. The advanced-farming lines are gated on g_optAdvancedFarming.

functions.name: TileInfo_DrawHerd
functions.comment: The herd half of TileInfo_Draw, and NOT a sowing forecast as first guessed. Draws only group 77's livestock lines: 5 'Calf births expected', 6 'Cow deaths expected', 7 'Change due to farming', 8..11 the four crowding levels, 0x10..0x12 the weather change, 0x13..0x17 disease/wolves/put down/over expectations, 0x1B 'Change due to eating' and 0x1C 'Overall change'. Group 77 mixes grain and herd text, so its index-0 label 'from' says nothing about which half a caller draws - only the indices do.

functions.name: TileInfo_DrawCastle
functions.comment: The castle block of TileInfo_Draw - the tile panel, not the build screen. Reads county +0x1C0 (castle type) into g_castleTaxBonus for group 71 string 0x10 'Boosts tax revenues by' and into g_castleGarrisonCap for 0xB 'Barracks for' + 0xC 'troops.'; that is the same cap FUN_004A79A3 tests a garrison against, which is what identifies the branch. With a garrison present it adds the unit's men (+0x168) and 0xD 'currently stationed here.', or 0x13 'Enemy troops are barracked here.', plus 0xE 'View these troops?' and a widget. Note the tables are one-based: DAT_004D8A0C is g_castleGarrisonCap - 4.

functions.name: Castle_DrawStatusBlock
functions.signature: void Castle_DrawStatusBlock(int county, int x, int y, int row)
functions.comment: The castle-under-construction block, drawn at a caller-chosen origin. L2.eng group 71: 0x10 tax bonus, 0xB/0xC barracks capacity, then county +0x1D0 with 6 'of stone needed,' and +0x1D4 with 7 'of wood needed.'; county +0x1A6 zero gives 0x11 'No castle building in progress.', otherwise county +0xE8 with 8 'will take'. Shared by TileInfo_DrawCastle and the county screen.

functions.name: CountyStrip_DrawCastleIcon
functions.comment: One county's castle cell on the county strip, not a castle screen. Picks a g_miscCtySheet frame from whether the castle is complete, and when county +0x1D0 or +0x1D4 (stone/wood still needed) is non-zero draws a materials icon plus L2.eng group 71 string 0x12 'Needed'. DAT_0056D68C is the strip row counter it advances on the way out.

functions.name: Screen_CastleBuild
functions.comment: Screen 0x1B, the castle chooser. Loads cas_back.256 / cas_back.pl8, the chosen castle's picture out of caspics.pl8 by DAT_004D2DD0[type], and cas_bits.pl8 into DAT_005533C4, then sets the DAT_005440B8 dirty flag and calls Screen_CastleBuildPanel.

functions.name: Screen_CastleBuildPanel
functions.comment: The stats panel of screen 0x1B, redrawn only when DAT_005440B8 is set. Names the selected type from L2.eng group 71 index DAT_0056D898 + 1 (1 'Wooden palisade.' .. 5 'Royal castle.'), then prints g_castleMaterial's stone and wood **net of the castle already there** (it subtracts g_castleMaterial[existing type]), g_castleWorkforce with 8 'will take' / 9 'to build.', g_castleTaxBonus with 0x10, g_castleGarrisonCap with 0xB/0xC, and 0xF 'Start construction?'. The four named constant tables all appearing together is what confirms this, rather than the group label, against the three other group-71 callers that are not this screen.

functions.name: Trade_DrawPanel
functions.comment: The widget pass of screen 0x66, the merchant trade panel. Draws essentially all of L2.eng group 68 - 1 'We receive', 5 'Buying', 6 'Selling', 8 'Total cost of', 9 'Buying price', 0xA 'Selling price', 0xC 'You have.', 0xE 'Purchase?', 0xF 'Sale?', and the four wrapped advice paragraphs 0x10..0x13 - beside the goods names in group 6.

functions.name: Screen_GreatestNoble
functions.comment: Screen 0x20, the standings. Loads grtnoble.256 / grtnoble.pl8 and flags.pl8 - the filename is the identification - and draws L2.eng group 35, the seven 'Most counties,' / 'Most castles,' / ... / 'Greatest noble,' categories, with string 7 'undecided.' where no realm leads. Walks the realms at stride 0x160 and labels each from g_playerNames.

functions.name: ScenarioList_Draw
functions.comment: The five-row scenario list box, with the selected row inverted and a proportional scrollbar thumb whose three segments are computed from the scroll offset, 5, and the total. Row text is L2.eng group 101, the 60 map slot names, but indexed *through* the byte table DAT_0050A460 rather than directly, so the visible order is not the group's order. What builds that table has not been read.

functions.name: SaveLoad_DrawStatus
functions.comment: The progress and error line of the load/save screens 0x35 and 0x36 - not the file browser. Switches on g_screenId to choose L2.eng group 40 string 2 'Loading game. Please wait.' or 3 'Saving game. Please wait.', and prints 4 'File error. Operation canceled.' on failure.

functions.name: Msg_DrawDiplomacy
functions.comment: The diplomatic letter window, message category 0x0C, dispatched from Msg_DrawWindow. Draws L2.eng group 109 string 0 'From' plus the sender's name, then switches on g_messageGroup - 0xF5 into eleven arms that land exactly on groups 245..255: 0 'A gift.' with a count, 1 and 2 'A communication' with the free-text body from g_diploLetter + realm*0xCA, 3 'Offer of alliance.', 4 the alliance termination, 5 'Plea for help' and 6 'Launch an attack.' with the county name from group 100, and 7..10 the four 'Reply to request' variants. Arms 3, 5 and 6 are the only ones that call Widget_Draw, and they are exactly the three whose text asks a question - a correspondence that could have failed eleven times and did not.

functions.name: Msg_DrawBeyondLetter
functions.comment: Message category 0x14. Byte-for-byte the layout of Msg_DrawDiplomacy, except that the sender is the literal string "Beyond" instead of g_playerNames[realm], only the free-text arms 1 and 2 (groups 246/247 'A communication') are handled, and no reply widget is drawn - so it is a letter the player cannot answer.

functions.name: Realms_AssignLords
functions.comment: New-game lord assignment, and not a name display as first guessed - it writes g_playerNames rather than drawing it. For each realm without one it picks an unused lord from g_lordChoice (indexed by the lord id and, off the deterministic path, by g_scenarioIndex & 3), stores the title in realm +0x07 and the lord id in +0x0A, takes the two colours from g_realmColour, and copies 16 bytes of L2.eng group 7 through Eng_Seek into g_playerNames + realm*0x2C. Group 7 is 'No player' / 'The Knight' / 'The Baron' / 'The Countess' / 'The Bishop'.

functions.name: Counties_PlaceSites
functions.comment: Once at map load, for every county 1..g_countyCount: County_FindTownTile into +0x70 and the anchor +0x6C/+0x6D, then County_PlaceResourceSites and County_PlaceBlacksmith, then County_FindCastleTile into +0x78 and the castle tile +0x74/+0x75. The order matters - the resource sites are placed relative to the town, and the castle plot is found afterwards.

functions.name: County_FindTownTile
functions.comment: Scans the 64x64 grid for this county's tiles with plane-0 bit **0x40** and no terrain yet, takes the 2x2 group, and leaves its x/y in DAT_0057C8D0 / DAT_0056846C. The result becomes the county anchor that County_FindFreeRoadTile searches around. Bit 0x40 is the county town: TileInfo_Draw prints L2.eng group 30 string 7 'County town.' for it, and the mercenary offer at county +0x1AD is advertised on it. See decisions.md C25.

functions.name: County_FindCastleTile
functions.comment: As County_FindTownTile but for plane-0 bit **0x80**, and it also stamps terrain 0x14 on the 2x2 it finds, saving the previous terrain frame to tile +6. Its result is county +0x74/+0x75, which is exactly the tile FUN_004A79A3 moves a garrisoning army onto - so bit 0x80 is the castle. Unit_TryEnterTile's special case for a 0x80 tile whose terrain is 0x14 is this stamp. See decisions.md C25.

functions.name: Eng_CopyString
functions.signature: void Eng_CopyString(int dest, int group, int index, int len)
functions.comment: Copies len bytes of L2.eng string (group, index) into a caller buffer, walking the group exactly as Eng_DrawString does. The fifth and last function that takes a literal (group, index) pair - the others are Eng_DrawString, Eng_Seek, Ui_DrawCentred and FUN_0040328E - and therefore the fifth place a call site names its own subject. Note the pair is at arguments 2 and 3 here, not 1 and 2.

globals.name: g_clipState
globals.comment: Clip state: 0 unclipped, 1 clipped left, 2 clipped right, 5 fully offscreen.

globals.name: g_clipVisibleWidth
globals.comment: Visible (clipped) sprite width.

globals.name: g_clipSrcSkip
globals.comment: Source bytes skipped per row = width - visible width.

globals.name: g_clipDstAdvance
globals.comment: Destination advance per row = screen stride - visible width.

globals.name: g_spriteWidth
globals.comment: Current sprite width.

globals.name: g_spriteHeight
globals.comment: Current sprite height.

globals.name: g_spriteDataOffset
globals.comment: Current source data offset within the PL8 buffer.

globals.name: g_screenStride
globals.comment: Screen stride, 640.

globals.name: g_blitRowCount
globals.comment: Blitter row counter. Not frame-record byte 0x0D - Clip_Vertical overwrites it before every blit, so the byte-0x0D load in Pl8_DrawFrame is dead.

globals.name: g_ddrawInterface
globals.comment: A DirectDraw interface pointer. It was NULL at the crash at 0x004522B5, which happened when the window was deactivated during startup under DxWnd.

globals.name: g_resourceTable
globals.comment: The game's resource directory: {char name[16]; u32 size;} records. Entries 0-31 are the map tile sets, eight layers x four seasons; 32-63 the zoom-2 sets; 64+ the battle-map sets. See docs/formats/maps-layers.md 1.1.

globals.name: g_scenarioIndex
globals.comment: The map slot, 0..59, used unshifted. Map_LoadLattice seeks slot * 0x80C1 (the whole slot stride), Eng_DrawString(101, g_scenarioIndex) indexes the 60 slot names in L2.eng group 101, and Minimap_Load takes the MAPnn.PL8 file from slot >> 2 and one of its four slots from slot & 3. An earlier note here said the low 2 bits select the season variant of the tile set: they do not - Gfx_LoadCountyMode takes the season from g_season.

globals.name: g_tiles
globals.comment: Runtime tile array, 4096 records x 8 bytes, index y*64 + x. +1 plane0 flags, +2 bank, +3 frame, +4 plane3, +5 unit index on this tile, +6 saved terrain frame, +7 county. See docs/formats/maps-layers.md 5.3.

globals.name: g_screenLattice
globals.comment: Runtime 129x65 dword screen lattice, row stride 0x104. Covered cells hold tileIndex*8; uncovered cells keep 0x0FFF0000 + backgroundFrame.

globals.name: g_countyCount
globals.comment: Highest county id on the loaded map, i.e. the county count. Set by Map_LoadPlanes as max(plane5) over ids below 0x11.

globals.name: g_units
globals.comment: Unit array, 151 records x 0x1A4 bytes, index 1..150 (0 unused); save block 5 is 63,420 bytes. Type at +0x08: 1 army, 2 revolting peasants, 3 merchant, 4 transport. Common: +0x00 owner, +0x07 sprite frame, +0x09 facing, +0x0A/+0x0B tile x/y, +0x0C tile offset, +0x10 county, +0x1C path length, +0x1D..+0x148 a 150-step (x,y) path, +0x14C move state, +0x14D on a road, +0x150 needs a destination, +0x151 destination county, +0x153 moves used, +0x154 move allowance (15 for an army, 10 otherwise). Army only: +0x11 home county, +0x14F army-name index into L2.eng group 93+owner, +0x155 starvation 0..5, +0x15C wages, +0x164 year formed, +0x166 morale, +0x168 total men, +0x16C+t*2 eleven i16 troop counts (0..6 campaign, 7..10 filled just before a battle), +0x182 three 6-byte siege-engine build records, +0x195/+0x196/+0x197 mercenary type/men/band, +0x198 garrison county, +0x199 besieged county, +0x19C siege seasons left. See docs/armies.md.

globals.name: g_lastUnitIndex
globals.comment: Index of the unit Unit_Spawn just allocated. Callers read it straight after the call to fill in the rest of the record.

globals.name: g_foundTileX
globals.comment: X of the tile the last Map_FindFree*TileNear search settled on.

globals.name: g_foundTileY
globals.comment: Y of the tile the last Map_FindFree*TileNear search settled on.

globals.name: g_merchantRoutes
globals.comment: The six merchant trade routes: 6 rows x 16 county ids, built from plane 4 on castle tiles. Row n is the itinerary of the merchant named by L2.eng group 5 string n. See docs/formats/plane4.md.

globals.name: g_merchantStartCounty
globals.comment: Six bytes: the county each merchant starts in, chosen by Merchant_PickStartCounties. A zero entry stops Merchant_SpawnAll.

globals.name: g_merchantCount
globals.comment: Number of merchants Merchant_SpawnAll actually placed, 1..6.

globals.name: g_playerStartTable
globals.comment: Player start table, {county, slot} byte pairs indexed by the plane-4 value on a settlement tile. See docs/formats/maps-layers.md 5.1.

globals.name: g_playerStartCount
globals.comment: Number of non-zero player start slots on the loaded map: 5, 4 or 2 across the shipped maps.

globals.name: g_county0_anchorX
globals.comment: X of county 0's anchor tile in the county record array (stride 0x300); County_FindFreeRoadTile searches around county*0x300 + this.

globals.name: g_county0_anchorY
globals.comment: Y of county 0's anchor tile, as above.

globals.name: g_turnPhase
globals.comment: Turn state machine phase, switched on by FUN_0049a010. Phase 6 step 1 is Merchant_AdvanceAll.

globals.name: g_turnPhaseStep
globals.comment: Step counter within the current turn phase; incremented on every FUN_0049a010 call.

globals.name: g_battleMen
globals.comment: Battle figure array, 81 records of 0x1B0 bytes, index 1..80 (0 unused). A figure is one drawn man representing g_menPerFigure real soldiers. +0x09 selected, +0x12 troop type, +0x13 owner is human, +0x18 facing 0..7, +0x1C cell byte offset, +0x20/+0x22 x,y, +0x24/+0x26 target x,y, +0x2C owner (0 = free slot), +0x31 state, +0x172 armour, +0x174 target figure, +0x178 owning unit, +0x17A side, +0x17E melee opponent, +0x189 move delay, +0x18B melee recovery interval, +0x197 strength band, +0x198 heavy-blow bonus, +0x19A hits, +0x19C melee attack, +0x1A0 men left. Full map in docs/battle.md. Eighty usable slots but eighty-one records of storage: every sweep is for (i = 1; i < 0x51; i++), so index 80 is live, and nothing else in the binary claims the space behind it.

globals.name: g_battleUnits
globals.comment: Battle unit array, 81 records of 0x34 bytes, index 1..80 (0 unused). A unit is what the player selects and orders. +0x00 owner (0 = free slot), +0x01 human controlled, +0x02 figure count, +0x03 side (0 or 4), +0x04/+0x06 first and last figure index, +0x08 category, +0x0F firing timer, +0x14 re-target countdown, +0x1A orders, +0x1E/+0x20 position, +0x22/+0x24 target, +0x2C ordered target figure, +0x30 target cell offset. Eighty usable slots but eighty-one records of storage: every sweep is for (i = 1; i < 0x51; i++), so index 80 is live, and nothing else in the binary claims the space behind it.

globals.name: g_missiles
globals.comment: Missile / effect array, 100 records of 0x4C bytes, index 1..100. +0x06 firing figure, +0x08 owner, +0x09 class (1 bow, 2 crossbow, 3 catapult, 5 fire, 7 falling figure), +0x0A/+0x0C position in 1/32 cell, +0x14/+0x16 cell x,y, +0x1C cell byte offset, +0x2F launch elevation, +0x36 distance flown, +0x38 range, +0x40 power.

globals.name: g_battlefield
globals.comment: Battlefield cell array, 80x80 records of 8 bytes, index (y*80 + x)*8. +0 terrain id, +1 flags (0x10 and 0x80 impassable), +2 flags, +3 graphic index, +4 elevation, +5 index of the figure standing here, +6 head of the missile list in this cell, +7 surface type (7 bridge, 10 and 17 burning, 15 woodland).

globals.name: g_curBattleMan
globals.comment: Index of the figure currently being updated. The whole figure state machine reads its subject from this global rather than from a parameter.

globals.name: g_otherBattleMan
globals.comment: Index of the other figure in the current interaction: the melee opponent, the missile target, or the figure being swapped with.

globals.name: g_curBattleUnit
globals.comment: Index of the unit currently being updated by Battle_UpdateAllUnits.

globals.name: g_lastBattleMan
globals.comment: Index of the figure BattleMan_Create just allocated.

globals.name: g_lastBattleUnit
globals.comment: Index of the unit BattleUnit_Alloc just allocated.

globals.name: g_lastMissile
globals.comment: Index of the missile Missile_Spawn just allocated.

globals.name: g_curMissile
globals.comment: Index of the missile Missile_Step is advancing.

globals.name: g_battleSizeClass
globals.comment: Battlefield size class 0..8, from the combined army size. It selects g_menPerFigure, the strength-band thresholds, and the burning-damage rate.

globals.name: g_menPerFigure
globals.comment: How many real soldiers one drawn figure stands for: 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512 or 1024 by size class. Reduced for a small army so that a side always gets at least 9 figures.

globals.name: g_battleIsSiege
globals.comment: Non-zero for a siege: selects the castle battlefield builder, the siege unit-order tables and Battle_RaiseSideSiege.

globals.name: g_localPlayer
globals.comment: The player index this machine controls. Compared against a unit owner to decide whose units are on the player side.

globals.name: g_strengthBand1
globals.comment: Men in a figure below which it drops to strength band 1 - 75% of a full figure.

globals.name: g_strengthBand2
globals.comment: Band 2 threshold - 50% of a full figure.

globals.name: g_strengthBand3
globals.comment: Band 3 threshold - about 19-25% of a full figure.

globals.name: g_absDx
globals.comment: Absolute x distance left by Dist_Manhattan / Dist_Chebyshev.

globals.name: g_absDy
globals.comment: Absolute y distance left by Dist_Manhattan / Dist_Chebyshev.

globals.name: g_troopStrengthWeight
globals.comment: Seven ints, the autocalc strength weight of one soldier by troop type: peasant 2, crossbowman 16, maceman 8, swordsman 13, pikeman 9, archer 13, knight 22. Used only for army strength comparisons, not by the real-time battle.

globals.name: g_troopBattleStats
globals.comment: Per troop type, 11 rows of 5 ints: max figures per unit, cell footprint, max figures per formation row, weapon class (index into g_missileStats), move delay in ticks.

globals.name: g_missileStats
globals.comment: Per weapon class, 4 rows of 5 ints: range in 1/8 cells, reload interval in ticks, sub-steps per tick, damage, sprite-bank offset. Class 0 melee (all zero), 1 bow (120, 50, 4, 50, 0), 2 crossbow (64, 100, 4, 200, 8), 3 catapult (160, 100, 4, 200, 16).

globals.name: g_meleeAttackTable
globals.comment: Melee attack value by troop type and strength band, 11 rows of 4 shorts. Peasant/crossbow/archer 5,4,3,2; mace and sword 15,12,10,6; pike 10,8,6,5; knight 20,15,11,6; siege engines all zero.

globals.name: g_menPerFigureTable
globals.comment: Nine ints indexed by battlefield size class: 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024 men per drawn figure.

globals.name: g_sizeClassLadder
globals.comment: Eight (threshold, size class) pairs mapping total men to the battlefield size class: 305, 609, 1217, 2433, 4865, 9729, 19457, 38913, then 8.

globals.name: g_siegeScaleLadder
globals.comment: Eight (threshold, value) pairs giving how many men one siege engine counts as when choosing the size class.

globals.name: g_strengthBandTable
globals.comment: Three ints per battlefield size class: the men-per-figure thresholds for strength bands 1, 2 and 3 - 75%, 50% and about 19-25% of a full figure.

globals.name: g_raiseOrder
globals.comment: The order in which troop types become units in a field battle: ram, oil, knight, sword, mace, pike, crossbow, archer, peasant, tower, catapult.

globals.name: g_raiseOrderSiege
globals.comment: The castle-defender raise order, eight troop types: oil, archer, crossbow, knight, peasant, sword, mace, pike. Catapults, towers and rams are absent.

globals.name: g_troopTickTable
globals.comment: Eleven function pointers indexed by troop type. Each reloads that troop per-tick constants - animation set, recovery interval, heavy-blow bonus, armour - and then tail-calls g_manStateTable[state].

globals.name: g_manStateTable
globals.comment: Eighteen figure-state handlers indexed by figure byte +0x31. Known: 2 dead, 4 melee, 5 idle/firing, 6 blocked, 7 look for melee, 12 siege engine attacking, 17 closing to attack.

globals.name: g_unitOrderTableField
globals.comment: Five unit order handlers for a field battle, indexed by unit category 0..4.

globals.name: g_unitOrderTableSiegeAtt
globals.comment: Nine unit order handlers for the siege attacker (unit side non-zero), indexed by unit category 0..8.

globals.name: g_unitOrderTableSiegeDef
globals.comment: Eleven unit order handlers for the siege defender (unit side zero), indexed by unit category 0..10.

globals.name: g_cellNeighbourOffsets
globals.comment: Eight ints, the battlefield cell byte offsets of the neighbours in direction order 0..7: -0x280, -0x278, +8, +0x288, +0x280, +0x278, -8, -0x288.

globals.name: g_troopsTable
globals.comment: The parsed TROOPS*.ENG table: short[35][2][5][11], row stride 0xDC, side stride 0x6E, difficulty stride 0x16. See docs/formats/eng.md and the correction in docs/battle.md.

globals.name: g_troopsAdvantage
globals.comment: The per-battle defensive advantage 0..10, one per TROOPS*.ENG row.

globals.name: g_troopsRowBase
globals.comment: Four ints, 0/10/20/35: the first g_troopsTable row for each battle category.

globals.name: g_battleArmyA
globals.comment: Index into g_units of the first army in the current battle. It is raised on side 4.

globals.name: g_battleArmyB
globals.comment: Index into g_units of the second army. It is raised on side 0, and is the side the castle-defender path is applied to in a siege.

globals.name: g_battleStrengthA
globals.comment: Autocalc strength of army A: sum of count[t] * g_troopStrengthWeight[t] over troop types 0..6.

globals.name: g_battleStrengthB
globals.comment: Autocalc strength of army B.

globals.name: g_debugSelectedMan
globals.comment: The figure index BattleDebug_Panel prints.

globals.name: g_pathCost
globals.comment: Pathfinder cost field, u16 per battlefield cell, index y*80 + x. 0 means unvisited, 1 the start cell, 998 (0x3E6) blocked.

globals.name: g_pathQueue
globals.comment: Pathfinder frontier, a circular queue of 0x1900 cell indices with head g_pathQueueHead and tail g_pathQueueTail.

globals.name: g_pathQueueHead
globals.comment: Read cursor of g_pathQueue.

globals.name: g_pathQueueTail
globals.comment: Write cursor of g_pathQueue; wraps at 0x1900.

globals.name: g_pathStepCost
globals.comment: Per-cell step cost the flood fill charges: a cell is only expanded once it has been reached this many times.

globals.name: g_pathVisitCount
globals.comment: How many times the flood fill has reached each cell, compared against g_pathStepCost.

globals.name: g_pathElevation
globals.comment: Per-cell elevation the flood fill and Path_Extract read; a step is only allowed between cells differing by at most 1.

globals.name: g_pathWaypoints
globals.comment: Scratch route built by Path_Extract: (x, y) byte pairs, at most 150, ordered destination-first. BattleMan_SetPath copies it into the figure.

globals.name: g_cellIndexNeighbours
globals.comment: Eight ints, the battlefield cell-index (not byte) deltas in direction order 0..7: -0x50, -0x4F, +1, +0x51, +0x50, +0x4F, -1, -0x51.

globals.name: g_counties
globals.comment: The county array: 17 records of 0x300 bytes, index 1..16 (0 unused). Base, count and stride all appear together in the multiplayer sync descriptor at 0x004D5B10 and in the save-block table at 0x004DE960.

globals.name: g_realms
globals.comment: Realm/player array: 6 records of 0x160 bytes, index 1..5. +0x00 AI step, +0x04 in play, +0x05 human, +0x07 lord, +0x28 empire tax happiness, +0x2B rank, +0x50 score, +0xFC army wages, +0x118 gold.

globals.name: g_countyFieldTiles
globals.comment: 17 x 20 u32 tile indices - the map tiles that are this county's farm fields. Save block 12 is exactly 1360 bytes = 17 * 80.

globals.name: g_saveBlocks
globals.comment: 225 {u32 address, u32 length} records terminated by a zero length; Save_Write dumps each in order. Sums to 267,028 bytes.

globals.name: g_syncBlocks
globals.comment: Seven 12-byte {count, stride, firstComparedOffset} descriptors used by Sync_CompareState and Sync_Checksum: counties (17, 0x300, 5), realms (6, 0x160, 6), units (151, 0x1A4, 0), battle men (81, 0x1B0, 18), missiles (101, 0x4C, 4), battle units (81, 0x34, 0).

globals.name: g_stateArrayPtrs
globals.comment: Eight pointers in the same order as g_syncBlocks: counties, counties, realms, units, battle men, missiles, battle units, battlefield. No reader was found; it corroborates every base address.

globals.name: g_season
globals.comment: Current season 1..4, used directly as the index into L2.eng group 29 (Spring, Summer, Autumn, Winter). Season_Advance sets it before running the economy, so the economy sees the season being entered.

globals.name: g_seasonNext
globals.comment: The season after g_season; the year rolls when the season that just ended was 4.

globals.name: g_seasonPrev
globals.comment: The previous value of g_season.

globals.name: g_year
globals.comment: Displayed year. 1268 on turn 1.

globals.name: g_yearNext
globals.comment: g_year + 1, staged for the next roll.

globals.name: g_turnCount
globals.comment: Turns elapsed; divides the happiness accumulator to give the running average.

globals.name: g_selectedCounty
globals.comment: The county the county panels display.

globals.name: g_weatherCounty
globals.comment: The county picked this season for the doubled local weather swing.

globals.name: g_optDifficulty
globals.comment: New-game difficulty 0..3 (easy/normal/hard/impossible, L2.eng group 103 indices 11..14). Scales AI gold, AI free resources and AI army wages.

globals.name: g_optAdvancedFarming
globals.comment: Advanced Farming (L2.eng group 102 index 0). When 0, weather is forced to Cloudy in every county and fertility is forced to 0.

globals.name: g_optArmiesEat
globals.comment: Armies Eat (L2.eng group 102 index 3). When 1, garrison and enemy troop counts are added to the county's food requirement.

globals.name: g_optTimeLimit
globals.comment: Turn time limit in seconds, 0 for none.

globals.name: g_grainYieldPerSack
globals.comment: 12. "Each sack planted will grow into 12 sacks" - the game's own FAQ text, L2.eng group 292 index 4.

globals.name: g_grainMaxSacksPerField
globals.comment: 10. The top of Grain_Sow's descending search; the manual's "up to 5 sacks" is wrong.

globals.name: g_grainLabourDivisorAdv
globals.comment: 5. Labour divisor used when Advanced Farming is on.

globals.name: g_grainLabourDivisor
globals.comment: 2. Labour divisor used when Advanced Farming is off.

globals.name: g_dairyPerHead
globals.comment: 5. People fed per head of the standing herd, without slaughter.

globals.name: g_foodPerHead
globals.comment: 10. People fed by one slaughtered animal.

globals.name: g_foodPerSack
globals.comment: 6. People fed by one sack of grain.

globals.name: g_birthRateLadder
globals.comment: 20 {population, percent} pairs from (40, 100) down to (3000, 1): the base birth rate falls as a county fills up.

globals.name: g_deathRateByHealth
globals.comment: Percent per season by health band 0..4: 35, 20, 8, 3, 0.

globals.name: g_deathRateBySeason
globals.comment: Percent per season, indexed 1..4: Spring 4, Summer 0, Autumn 2, Winter 8.

globals.name: g_healthDeltaTable
globals.comment: int[6][5]: change to the health meter by ration level 0..5 and health band 0..4. Row 3 (Normal) is the first that is positive.

globals.name: g_healthBandLadder
globals.comment: Five {threshold, band} pairs: 10/0, 35/1, 65/2, 90/3, 100/4.

globals.name: g_healthHappiness
globals.comment: Happiness per season by health band: -10, -5, 0, +1, +2 for Diseased, Sick, Average, Good, Perfect (L2.eng group 20).

globals.name: g_herdWeatherPct
globals.comment: Percent change to the herd by weather 0..5: Frost -2, Drought -10, Sunny +5, Cloudy 0, Storms -5, Flooding -10.

globals.name: g_rationTable
globals.comment: Six {divisor, multiplier} pairs: (1,0) None, (4,1) Quarter, (2,1) Half, (1,1) Normal, (1,2) Double, (1,3) Triple - exactly L2.eng group 21.

globals.name: g_eventTable
globals.comment: The random-event id ring Event_RollAll draws from; 0 means no event.

globals.name: g_armyHappinessCost
globals.comment: int[102] happiness cost of raising an army, indexed by the PERCENTAGE of the county's population taken rather than by the number of men: 0, 1, 1, 1, 2 ... 90 at half the county, then a flat 101 from index 61 up. FUN_004A5003 reads it unbounded, so a county under 50 people indexes past the end into g_goodsPrice and gets a free army. 0x004D8778 + 102 * 4 is exactly 0x004D8910, which is what fixes the length.

globals.name: g_goodsPrice
globals.comment: Merchant base price per good id, 15 entries in L2.eng group 6 order: -, grain 2, cattle 12, sheep 0, ale 1, wool 0, iron 1, stone 2, timber 1, pikes 13, bows 16, maces 10, crossbows 24, swords 23, mail 44.

globals.name: g_goodsStock
globals.comment: A second 15-entry table on the same good ids: 1000 grain, 100 cattle, 200 sheep, 100 ale, 500 wool, 100 iron, 100 stone, 200 timber, 500 each weapon. Reads like the quantity a merchant carries.

globals.name: g_weaponCost
globals.comment: Six {wood, iron} pairs: crossbow 6/10, mace 4/4, sword 3/10, pike 6/3, bow 13/0, armour 4/18. Debited by Industry_Produce.

globals.name: g_castleMaterial
globals.comment: Five {wood, stone} pairs: palisade 400/40, motte and bailey 800/80, Norman keep 200/1000, stone castle 400/2000, royal castle 800/3000.

globals.name: g_castleWorkforce
globals.comment: Man-seasons per castle type, each value stored twice: 200, 400, 800, 1500, 2500.

globals.name: g_castleGarrisonCap
globals.comment: Troops a castle can hold: 150, 200, 200, 400, 600.

globals.name: g_castleTaxBonus
globals.comment: Percent tax bonus by castle type: 50, 75, 100, 125, 150 - the same ratios as Tax_CollectAll's 480/560/640/720/800 over the castle-less 320.

globals.name: g_castleFreeArchers
globals.comment: Archers a newly finished castle is given: 50, 150, 150, 200, 300.

globals.name: g_aiPersonality
globals.comment: Per-AI-lord behaviour parameters: FOUR records of 240 bytes (0x50 x 3, only the first row used), lords 1..4 = the Knight, the Baron, the Countess and the Bishop (L2.eng group 7). Addressed as base + (lord * 3 - 3) * 0x50. The record's +0x00 is the farming style AI_ManageFields dispatches on and +0x04 the AI_SetTaxRates ladder selector; an earlier revision gave this address as the +0x04 field. There is no fifth record: 0x004D8A58 + 4 * 240 = 0x004D8E18, and what begins there is the campaign-progression table FUN_00499E5D reads with a 0x20 stride. Traced fields are in docs/diplomacy.md 8.4.

globals.name: g_aiGoldGrant
globals.comment: int[5][4] free gold per turn by AI lord and difficulty for a realm holding three or more counties: 0/0/0/0, 0/400/700/1200, 100/500/800/1400, 0/400/700/1200, 250/600/1100/1800.

globals.name: g_aiGoldGrantSmall
globals.comment: The same shape, used when the realm holds fewer than three counties.

globals.name: g_aiStrengthAdvantage
globals.comment: The AI's view of the battle, recomputed every 101 frames by Battle_UpdateStrengthAdvantage: weighted AI men as a percentage of weighted human men, minus 100, plus a -10..+21 jitter outside deterministic play. Every field and siege handler branches on it. It is one global for the whole battle, not per side and not per unit.

globals.name: g_aiAggressionThreshold
globals.comment: Set to 5 by Rules_InitConstants and read only by the three field order handlers: above this advantage they attack, at or below it they hold and skirmish.

globals.name: g_aiSortieThreshold
globals.comment: Set to 260 by Rules_InitConstants and read only by the four siege-defender handlers: above this advantage the garrison lays the drawbridge patch and charges out.

globals.name: g_aiAdvantageTimer
globals.comment: Frame counter in Battle_UpdateAllUnits; at 101 it triggers Battle_UpdateStrengthAdvantage and resets.

globals.name: g_aiCommitCounter
globals.comment: Zeroed by Battle_Start.
